concepts.def: Belief in one God only; foundational to Christianity, Judaism and Islam, in contrast to polytheism, the belief in many gods.
The belief that God is all-powerful, able to do anything consistent with the divine nature, shown in creation and miracles.
The belief that God is all-loving and supremely good, caring for creation; questioned by the existence of evil and suffering.
God is transcendent, existing beyond space and time, yet also immanent, present and active within the world and human lives.
The Christian belief that the one God exists as three persons — Father, Son and Holy Spirit — distinct yet united in one being.
God making the divine known to humans: general revelation through nature and conscience, and special revelation through scripture, prophets and religious experience.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Beliefs about Deity — a core area of GCSE Religious Studies.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Beliefs about Deity brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Beliefs about Deity.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does it mean to describe God as omnipotent?
options: All-powerful
All-knowing
Present everywhere
All-loving

mcqs.q: What does 'transcendent' mean when applied to God?
options: Existing beyond space, time and the physical universe
Limited by the laws of nature
Identical with the physical universe
Visible in human form today

mcqs.q: Which term describes belief in one God?
options: Monotheism
Polytheism
Atheism
Agnosticism

mcqs.q: Which of these is an example of special revelation?
options: God speaking through scripture or a prophet
Inferring a creator from the beauty of nature
Reasoning that the universe had a cause
Observing the regularity of the seasons

mcqs.q: Does the doctrine of the Trinity mean Christians believe in three gods?
options: No — the Trinity teaches one God in three persons (Father, Son, Holy Spirit), distinct in person but united in one being; Christianity remains monotheistic.
The Trinity refers to the three wise men at Jesus' birth.
Christians believe in three separate gods.
Omnipotent means God exists only in heaven.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between omnipotent and omniscient?
options: Omnipotent means God exists only in heaven.
The Trinity refers to the three wise men at Jesus' birth.
Omnipotent means God knows everything that will happen.
Omnipotent means all-powerful; omniscient means all-knowing. They are distinct attributes of God, often listed together with omnibenevolence (all-loving).

mcqs.q: Can God be both transcendent and immanent?
options: Yes — most theists hold both: God is beyond the universe (transcendent) yet also present and active within it (immanent), for example through answered prayer.
Transcendent and immanent are two different gods in Christianity.
Omnipotent means God exists only in heaven.
If God is transcendent and outside the universe, God cannot also act within the world.
